items.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: Bob Megel was playing first trumpet, I was playing first trombone. Aaron came into conduct his theater music and I think that’s the only time I ever worked for him, or with him.

ctx.x: Right. When you think back early in your career, was there certain milestones that you reflect on now that were important, as like Gerry Mulligan or—

Very much so. I came into the business with the ability to play the trombone. I played a Broadway show, I did the music hall, I did the operas and the classical music. I did do Larry Elgart, on bass trombone by the way so I was playing first trombone on the classical end of it and I was playing bass trombone on the jazz end let’s say, not really jazz at that point but on the dance band end of it. When — a tremendous milestone was Gerry Mulligan. I remember walking, I was at the union and Dick Hickson, who is a…

jazz band.” I said, “Well I’m quick.” He says, “Come on down.” That was it. That was the end of the conversation. I went down to the rehearsal. I sat next to Brookmeyer. Now Gerry, letting me into his band was a big moment for me. Because I stayed with the band for three years, I re-joined the band eighteen years later and stayed for another year or so, and musically it was a wonderful experience.
